title: In my tiny Pong, a perfect defender loses on the sixth shot

lines.title: THE BET
lines.narration_text: In my tiny Pong, a perfect defender loses on the sixth shot, and nobody makes a mistake. Here is why.
lines.visual_intent: Hook on frame one: the field fills the safe area, the rally already moving; big counter at the top.
lines.status: MODEL (paddle speed 2.0; first undefendable shot is the sixth).

lines.title: THE CONTEXT
lines.narration_text: Pong is two paddles and one ball. An essay I read says it has no perfect defense, and I wanted to know when that is true. So I built the smallest Pong I could. I'm Tanmay Kulkarni, in for Humanitarians AI.
lines.visual_intent: Same scene, the ball easing between the paddles; a settings chip in the safe area (858 by 525, paddle 60, plus five percent per shot); the two essay phrases as small captions.
lines.status: ESSAY (two phrases only); MODEL (settings on screen).

lines.title: THE COUNT
lines.narration_text: Watch the rally. Shot one. Shot two. Shot three. Shot four. Shot five. All defended. Shot six. The ball goes past.
lines.visual_intent: Counter 1 to 6 in step with the words; the ball's path to the top edge each shot; on six the paddle stops 8.4 px short.
lines.status: SIM (break index 5 at paddle speed 2.0; gap 8.4 px).

lines.title: THE TIME
lines.narration_text: The defender can see where the ball is going. What it lacks is time, because the ball gets five percent faster on every shot.
lines.visual_intent: A timer bar for one crossing shrinks with each shot; the ball's speed number steps up.

lines.title: THE TWO BARS
lines.narration_text: Two bars explain it. The first is how far the paddle can travel while the ball crosses. The second is how far the worst shot makes it go, about half the field. If the first is longer, a perfect defense exists.
lines.visual_intent: The two bars grow into view over the field (can travel 286 px at shot one; must travel 232.5 px), the line between them.

lines.title: THE CLOCK
lines.narration_text: But the crossing keeps shrinking, so the first bar sinks. On the sixth shot it drops below the line, by about eight pixels. The arithmetic says shot six, and a search that tries every aim agrees. Nobody made a mistake. The rally ran out of time.
lines.visual_intent: The first bar sinks shot by shot (286 to 224 px); on six it crosses the line; the gap lit; two ticks land on shot six.
lines.status: SIM (224 vs 232.5 at shot six; predicted 4.24 speed-ups, sixth; found sixth).

lines.title: THE LIMIT
lines.narration_text: It is only a model, with no spin and no real machine. But it shows that no perfect defense is true here only because the ball speeds up.
lines.visual_intent: MODEL, NOT A MACHINE in the safe area; the no-speed-up row runs past the frame edge.
lines.status: SIM (no speed-up: paddle speeds 2.0 and 3.0 held for 200 shots).

lines.title: THE FILM
lines.narration_text: The full film is called The Rally Has a Clock: When Is No Perfect Defense True in Pong?
lines.visual_intent: The title in the safe area; the scene settles back to the first frame (loop-friendly).
lines.status: Exact searchable title as in the long film's YouTube title.
